title: Maximum Mod Product of String Split
statement:
You are given a string `S` made only of the digits `0`-`9`. Split it into exactly two **non-empty** parts: a left part (a prefix) and a right part (the remaining suffix). Read the left part as a decimal number `A` and the right part as a decimal number `B`. Leading zeros are allowed inside a part and simply do not change its value (for example, `"05"` is the number `5`).

Among all possible split points, find the maximum value of `(A mod 7) × (B mod 7)`.

The string can be very long, so `A` and `B` will not fit in any built-in integer type.
inputFormat: A single line containing the digit string `S`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum value of `(A mod 7) × (B mod 7)` over all splits.
constraints: S consists only of the characters `0`-`9`

examples.explanation: Splitting as `1 | 25` gives 1 × 4 = 4. Splitting as `12 | 5` gives (12 mod 7) × (5 mod 7) = 5 × 5 = 25, which is the best.
Every split has a part made entirely of zeros: `1 | 000` gives 1 × 0, `10 | 00` gives 3 × 0, `100 | 0` gives 2 × 0. So the maximum is 0.

hints: Do not convert the parts to big integers. You only need each part modulo 7.
The value of every prefix modulo 7 can be built left to right: `r = (r * 10 + digit) % 7`.
For suffixes, sweep from the right and add `digit * 10^k` modulo 7, keeping the power of 10 modulo 7 as you go. Then combine prefix and suffix residues at every split point.
